answer: The useful question is not who joined, but what each join costs. Registration is priced by a congestion auction: as the arrival rate of new keys rises, the copper fee climbs until demand falls back. Fees flow to the vertex pool and the forge price history is public. A ring arriving in bulk bids against itself and pays more per seat than the trickle of honest newcomers, so the protocol converts an attack into revenue for the agents already doing real work.
